The tool appears to infer "last unspent unit" from the has-acted flags being cleared plus the phase byte moving, which is exactly what a chapter transition also looks like — the same ambiguity fe7_act's own 'wait' documentation warns about, resolved the wrong way here. This is the dangerous failure shape: had I believed it, I would have gone looking for why six units silently lost their turn. Note also that Wil's max HP is printed as 24/24 in this line but 23/23 everywhere before it — he levelled up on the kill, which is fine, but it means the line mixes a pre- and post-level-up reading without saying so.

detail: The whole run's shape was set by one thing the tools do not do: fe7_act commits a unit's turn in a single call, so ordering a nine-unit march through a one-tile funnel means nine sequential calls per turn, each of which I have to pre-compute destinations for BY HAND against a cost grid I can only see for one unit at a time. Concrete instances this run: (a) I repeatedly issued a move that was refused because an ally I had not moved yet was standing on the destination — fe7_act(#4 Wil, 3, 5) was refused with "OCCUPIED by a ally unit (slot #11)", and I had to reorder; (b) crossing the (13,5)-(13,6) mountain funnel took turns 6, 7 and 8 to file eight units through, and I hand-computed each unit's stopping tile from the previous unit's vacated tile; (c) fe7_reachable's grid is only valid until anyone moves, so after every single fe7_act every other unit's grid is stale and I plan the rest of the turn from memory. It worked — the chapter is won on turn 9 with no deaths — but the reason job 1 went fine is that I spent most of my thinking on tile arithmetic rather than on tactics.
